items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18
items.q: And I quit, I quit in St. Louis. That's when I started working with Faith.

ctx.x: for it, can't you? Putting a snake in my pocket. He says, I'd scare anybody. And the guys in the audience was hollering, hey doc, how about them bull constrictors? That's what made it look so ridiculous. But anyway, he didn't fire me then. I didn't quit the show until, uh,

How long did you stay with the show together? Oh God, not, not too long, maybe four or five months. Four or five months? Mm-hmm. And I quit, I quit in St. Louis. That's when I started working with Faith. What else you would start to tell us about, uh, Charlie and him? About what the, what all you did on the show? Uh, he says, you know, the doc would come out first and throw out the, the court. Well, he would, the doc was, uh, more or less, uh, an emcee and a straight man. After you, you did your acts, uh, we, we…

Now, folks, he says, now, you see this poor fella here? This poor fella is practically dying on his seat. And this doc, help me, doc. Help me. Help me. I'm dying. Now, he says, I will show you. He says, I'll give you a demonstration here. Give this fella a shot of this moon's tonic.
